title: Install or configure retained Cast state
summary: Install Cast and its matching provider bundle. Initialize retained private state, inspect local diagnostics and accounting, change retained configuration or source metadata, or reconcile employer ownership without collecting or migrating data.
use_when: Cast should be installed, initialized, diagnosed or explicitly reconfigured.
The caller needs to inspect retained local accounting, configuration or source diagnostics.
Existing ATS or older JSON-LD records need the supported employer-ownership correction without resetting paid usage.
do_not_use_when: A current discovery run or a read-only employer/job export is the requested outcome.
A schedule, provider subscription purchase, credential change, database deletion or downstream action is intended.
outcome: An installed matching program/documentation release, initialized Cast state, supported diagnostic result, explicitly replaced configuration or transactionally reconciled employer ownership.

interfaces.label: Clear a retained source enabled setting

effects: Direct installation stages an immutable wrapper, Rust payload, Rust installer and exact provider bundle and advances only Cast-owned command/provider selectors. The deploy recipe also initializes state and applies supplied configuration. It creates no schedule.

Init creates private schema-two current state when missing and preserves existing schema-one discovery state without migration. Explicit configuration changes update retained settings; diagnostic reads do not start searches.
The installed wrapper sources ~/.zshrc with output suppressed and starts the Rust payload with only the documented environment and two provider keys.

Source add retains an explicit source. Ordinary websites may use an existing company ID or a hostname candidate; supported ATS URLs use their canonical provider/tenant owner and reject --company-id. Source disable clears its retained enabled setting and preserves evidence. No remote source is fetched.

In schema-one state, ownership reconciliation applies current adapter rules to stored ATS source/job associations, sets older or shared-host JSON-LD jobs to unknown, restores affected search-candidate names and clears shared-host domains, website URLs and aliases. It preserves IDs, metadata, usage, runs and query checkpoints. In schema-two state it reports zero changes and preserves accepted employers, operators and snapshot revision.

The Cast deployment recipe initializes missing state without collection and applies an explicitly supplied complete config file. Existing records and consumed budgets remain. No collection schedule is created.
authority: Cast owns its installation, state schema, configuration validation and local allowance accounting.
The caller chooses collection policy and provider accounts; provider balances are managed by each provider.
success: Installation selects the supplied commands and documentation without executable probes.
Initialization, configuration or diagnosis returns its documented local outcome.

Ownership repair returns moved_sources, moved_jobs, quarantined_jobs, renamed_candidates and cleared_shared_identities counts after one committed transaction; changed jobs/companies retain identity and gain material revisions.
failure_and_recovery: Deployment refuses foreign selectors and stale expected selections. A failed instruction retains completed changes for explicit recovery.
Program rollback preserves current domain state. Do not hand-edit database rows.
Configuration changes do not purchase credits or reset accumulated usage. Diagnostic key presence does not establish provider authentication or current availability.
privacy: Keys remain in the caller environment and user-owned shell configuration, outside the Cast database and installed provider bundle.
State and exports may reveal personal search interests and should remain private.
does_not_authorize: Selecting jobs for the user, creating CRM cases or application packets, sending email, submitting applications, invoking an agent or browser, or enabling a schedule.
Changing provider billing, automatic purchases, another product installation, or deleting retained state.

consumers.statement: The current user may follow this procedure for Cast program installation or recovery, state initialization, configuration, diagnosis, source controls and supported ownership repair.

preconditions.statement: Select the intended home/state, use a supplied candidate and trusted tested installer for program work, preserve complete configuration and budgets, and stop callers before repair.

inputs.statement: Inputs are exact candidate/bundle or canonical retained-release paths, selected home/state, a complete intended schema-one config file, source URL/ID and optional ordinary-website company identity.

outputs.statement: Supported reads verify command identity, configuration, local diagnosis, source ownership/enrollment and ownership-repair counts after the intended operation.

data_semantics.statement: Artifact selection, local readiness and current external provider success are separate outcomes. State and install feature contracts own their full meanings.

identity_and_units.statement: Verify exact release selection, selected state directory, source/job identity and repair counts. cast.state owns budget units and cast.discovery.explore owns retained revisions.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Checks describe selected local artifacts and state at invocation. Repair counts describe the committed selected transaction, not external collection coverage.
Installation and local diagnosis do not establish current provider balance, authentication or successful collection.

access.statement: Use supported tested installer and current-user CLI interfaces. Keep program paths user-owned and state/exports/diagnostics private. Chancery reading is optional installed documentation and performs no product work.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Follow the owning feature's locked installation, state and reconciliation boundaries. Verify matching selectors after installation or recovery and preserve consumed budgets and prior state.

operational_limits.statement: This procedure starts no collection and creates no schedule, model job or downstream application result. Missing state uses the accepted current model; existing data is not migrated. It authorizes no provider purchase, credential replacement, destructive reset or hand repair.
Stop on foreign public selectors, displaced active ownership or unsupported recovery.

Deploy accepts one bounded schema-two recipe request on stdin. The product command owns its setup; the shared executor uses process exit status only. Deployment runs no application execution probe, native-signature audit, maintenance hold, drain, or automatic rollback.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: The operation retains its ID and retires all collection. Required feature contracts provide complete explanations. Store supports legacy and current state with the existing read schemas. Program recovery restores no state; schema-one-only programs cannot open schema-two state, and older programs can reject automatic_excluded_ats.

reliances.statement: Program selection and recovery follow Cast-owned release metadata and selector rules.
State setup and changes follow Cast-owned configuration, source-control, budget and repair rules.
Verification uses Cast's retained record and export meanings.

steps: Select the intended operator home and state directory, inspect current configuration and choose the authorized local operation.
Install a supplied binary and bundle through a trusted tested candidate, then verify command identity and register usage.
Initialize missing state, inspect readiness and complete configuration, and explicitly apply only the intended complete replacement.
Add or disable an exact source and verify ownership and enabled state without treating enrollment as collection success.
Stop writers before supported ownership reconciliation and verify counts, associations and retained accounting through reads.
Recover a canonical retained release. Program recovery leaves discovery state unchanged.
checkpoints: The tested candidate and provider release match and all selectors belong to Cast.
Configuration and source effects are explicit and consumed budgets remain retained.
Local readiness is separate from provider authentication, allowance and collection success.
Ownership repair preserves stable IDs, usage, run history, coverage and cursors.
Program recovery leaves state unchanged and the selected program accepts its configuration.
adaptation: Use the selected installed release and state configuration; do not infer live readiness from catalog presence.
Read product/show/resolve after installation when Chancery is available; Cast remains useful without a reader.
stop_when: A public selector is foreign, an expected selection changed, or an active writer would be displaced.
Proposed recovery requires unsupported row edits, destructive reset or an incompatible program/state pair.
